title: The other owner and the coat
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wednesday. The laundromat owner looks at the coat and says nothing about washing it. She runs a laundromat. She says nothing. Wood notices her saying nothing. She says she's seen coats. He says what kind. She says the kind you don't wash.

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner looking at WOOD's coat. Not saying anything. The dryers. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner looking at a young man's stained chore coat without comment, dryers turning behind her, black and white, no words

balloons.text: You're not going to say it.

image.prompt: a young man noticing a silence, black and white, no words
a laundromat owner in a cardigan, level, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The rack. The coat. The two owners agree without meeting: leave it. The strip: twelve strokes. It's counting down.

image.prompt: a young man in a chore coat standing in a laundromat with a small dog, drawn in twelve sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: 'The kind you don't wash.' Both owners agree. Twelve strokes.
